Under these non-exclusive constraints, Google\'s $20 billion per year default search payments to Apple remain permitted [15]. The DOJ is currently appealing this order [16].\n*   **DOJ Ad Tech Antitrust Remedies**: In April 2025, Judge Leonie Brinkema ruled that Google operated an illegal ad-tech monopoly [17]. The DOJ has requested a structural divestiture of Google\'s AdX exchange, where publishers pay Google a 20% transaction fee [18]. The income statement is one of the three key financial statements\xa0produced to evaluate the financial condition of a company—the other two being the balance sheet and the cash flow statement. A company\'s income statement presents investors and analysts with a picture of its overall profitability and financial health by outlining its revenue and expenses. Information from the income statement is typically a major focus whenever a company reports its quarterly and annual earnings. It is the most direct aspect of the income statement and immediately provides an assessment of the company’s marketplace performance. Profit margin is a common measure of the degree to which a company or a particular business activity makes money. Expressed as a percentage, it represents the portion of a company’s sales revenue that it retains as a profit after subtracting all of its costs. Profitability ratios are often the first thing investors look at before investing in a company, and the most popular and widely watched of them all is profit margins. A profit margin reflects the money a company retains as profit from its revenue. Put simply, it is the amount that a company earns relative to its revenue—usually expressed as a percentage. The income statement is one of the three key financial statements\xa0produced to evaluate the financial condition of a company—the other two being the balance sheet and the cash flow statement.
